Ticket #23 — Product Returns & Exchanges

Difficulty: Medium

Context

You maintain a shop's returns desk. An order line records the purchased SKU (product identifier), quantity, and original unit price in cents. A refund returns money; an exchange returns the original item and consumes replacement stock. Return limits combine earlier refunds and exchanges for the same order line.

Practice report

Order o1 has line l1: 3 coats at 2500 cents each. Current stock is coat=1, shirt=4, with no missing replacement SKU. Request one coat exchange using process("r1", "o1", "l1", 1, "exchange", "missing") through the route adapter.

Observation after rejection Current starter Expected
Route status 409 409
Stock coat=2, shirt=4 coat=1, shirt=4
Saved return cases None None

A failed exchange must not make an additional coat available for sale.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Validate a new nonempty return ID, an existing order line, a positive integer quantity excluding booleans, and an action of refund or exchange.
  • Returned quantity across earlier refunds and exchanges plus the new request cannot exceed the purchased quantity. Line IDs are scoped to their order.
  • A refund restores the original SKU's quantity and returns exactly quantity * original_unit_price cents.
  • An exchange requires a replacement SKU and enough replacement units. Success restores the original units, consumes the replacement units, returns zero refund cents, and records one completed return case.
  • Any rejected request leaves stock and return records unchanged. Stock never becomes negative.
  • A reused return ID is rejected with no second effect, including an exact replay.

Out of Scope

Keep the local inventory and returned refund_cents result. Real payment refunds, shipping, return eligibility dates, and exchange price differences are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the unavailable replacement, then compare a successful exchange and refund. Add tests for split returns reaching the purchase limit, replay, and the same line ID on separate orders. Assert inventory, case records, and refund amounts.
